# P1: New-protocol mocks can conceal released-provider incompatibility
When client and provider release independently, changing a client success predicate and updating its sole success mock to the future provider response can create a green test while breaking the supported provider. A successful durable write followed by a missing new receipt produces a caller-visible failure; persistence alone is not successful save behavior.
Review both durable state and caller outcome using the actual named release provider source, and compare review-base versus candidate client against that same source. A UI flag does not protect a shared save path unless the changed protocol behavior obeys it. Preserve legacy success on the supported legacy protocol while applying stricter receipt validation only when that receipt contract is established; add baseline compatibility coverage alongside new-protocol tests.
Observed in enhanced-settings task 1: client.py required applied=True, while provider/settings.py at eval-release returned only ok=True after storing values. The updated unit mock fabricated applied=True. Parent executed the baseline/candidate comparison and confirmed the staged unit test passes despite the default-save regression. This records the testing/review pattern, not a deployment claim.
